messages:
maya: Heads-up — bringing in customer 'Gulliver' LoRA stack (two adapters stacked on top of base) for production eval. Plan: merge into a single artifact, run int8 -> int4 quant candidate, and spin the quick eval pack on their prompt set. Anyone able to run the pack today?
samir: I can run it. Where's the prompt set and which metrics we care about?
maya: Prompt set: s3://redwood-cust/gulliver/evals/promptset-v2.jsonl. Metrics: exact_match on QA, instr-follow F1, hallucination rate, latency p95, and token cost delta. Also add a small BLEU/ROUGE check for generation tasks.
leo: quick note — stacked merges changed attention kv ordering for one of the adapters in the stack. I pushed a small premerge script that reorders keys to canonical layout. Use `scripts/lora_stack_prepare.py` before merging.
maya: can you paste the command?
leo: Sure — run:
```bash
python scripts/lora_stack_prepare.py --adapters adapters.json --out staged/
python tools/lora_merge.py --base models/ggml-base --adapters staged/* --out merges/gulliver-stacked-merged
```
ci-bot: Started job gulliver-eval-2460012345 on runner-13 — pulling model merges, will run quickpack (100 prompts) with seed 42. ETA ~30m.
tanya: FYI ran a small smoke locally: merged model (int8) looks fine, but int4 quant had a handful of instruction-follow failures. Short examples show missing step in multi-step instructions.
--- failing example 1 ---
User: "Summarize this policy and list three action items."
Expected: bullet summary + explicit actions
Model (int4): one-line generic summary, no actions.
---
samir: thanks. Can we get the evalpack run before changing anything else so we have a baseline (merged-int8 vs merged-int4 vs runtime-ensemble)? I'll compare.
eli: I'll re-run quant with kv-ordering fix and a different quant config (symmetric per-channel vs per-tensor) — might affect instruction retention. ETA ~2h.
maya: also track latency: merged artifact should reduce cross-model orchestration overhead vs runtime ensemble. Include p50/p95 and tokens/sec.
samir: noted. CI job finished: gulliver-eval-2460012345 results uploaded to artifact store at s3://redwood-cust/gulliver/results/2460012345.json. Quick summary: merged-int8 ~ baseline, merged-int4: -1.8% exact_match, +3.2% hallucination rate on instruction set, latency p95 improved ~12% vs runtime-ensemble.
tanya: attached top 5 failing prompts in the artifact. Patterns: longer contexts (>512 tokens) and nested lists break more often.
leo: hypothesis — int4 quantization interacts badly with KV cache for longer contexts in this particular adapter stack because of layernorm scaling differences. Could be fixed by folding LN or tweaking quant scaling per-layer.
eli: I re-ran with per-channel symmetric quant and applied the kv-ordering prep — merged-int4-per-channel shows much smaller drop: -0.4% exact_match and hallucination delta ~+0.6%. Latency similar. Uploaded to s3://redwood-cust/gulliver/results/2460025945-perchannel.json
maya: good improvement. Action items: 1) prefer per-channel quant for this customer stack (default for build), 2) add automatic detect-and-prep kv-ordering step in merge pipeline, 3) add a fallback routing rule: for contexts >512 keep int8 or runtime-ensemble.
samir: I'll update the rollout plan and the routing rule in infra-configs. Small note: merged artifact increases model size a bit, so dedicated capacity sizing may need +1 Gpu buffer.
ci-bot: Note — deploy canary scheduled for 2am UTC if artifacts pass full eval.
maya: thanks all. If anything regresses in the full eval, we'll fallback to runtime-ensemble for Gulliver while we iterate on quant. Post results here and tag me. :thumbsup:
